This position will work closely with the Operations Director to collect all impact metrics across IN-PLACE activities, conduct rigorous data cleaning, promote dissemination, and work with the Research Core to assemble future grant proposals to sustain IN-PLACE. Organization Summary Statement: The Center for Substance Use, Addiction & Health Research (CESAR) at the University of Maryland, College Park, was created in 1990 as a college-wide interdisciplinary research center. CESAR is dedicated to addressing the problems substance use disorders may create for individuals, families, and communities in Maryland and around the world. Our practical action-oriented studies and evaluations focus on improving access to treatment for substance use disorders and supporting long-term recovery. Our work spans the State of Maryland, including several projects in DC and Baltimore as well as reaching rural areas of both Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore. In addition, CESAR has several clinical trials located in Cape Town, South Africa. IN-PLACE is an interdisciplinary initiative advancing community-engaged research on the relationships between people, place, environment, and health. Through partnerships across the University of Maryland and communities statewide, IN-PLACE conducts research on equitable access to nature, develops and evaluates nature-based health interventions, and translates evidence into education, workforce development, and community programming. Key Responsibilities: ● Supporting data collection across all IN-PLACE cores ● Supporting the administration of the IN-PLACE seed grant program, including assisting with calls for proposals, application tracking, review coordination, award administration, and program evaluation. ● Providing evaluation support to the Community and Campus cores, including generating pilot data for future proposals and demonstrating the impact of IN-PLACE activities ● Working closely with the Operations Director to collect all impact metrics across IN-PLACE activities ● Conducting rigorous data cleaning and data quality assurance ● Assisting in the implementation of effective data flow and tracking systems across cores ● Promoting dissemination of findings to academic and community audiences ● Working with the Research Core to assemble future grant proposals to sustain IN-PLACE ● Supporting qualitative and quantitative data collection, management, and analysis ● Assisting with administrative responsibilities to support IN-PLACE programming and events In addition to work on active IN-PLACE activities, additional duties include but are not limited to: assisting with presentations for scientific conferences and manuscript/grant preparation, developing research protocols and preparing IRB submissions, supporting oversight and mentorship of students in the lab, and capacity building to support training of other team members. JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY Dance Instructor MCC’s Continuing Education Division is seeking enthusiastic, experienced, and knowledgeable Dance Instructors to provide engaging and enriching learning opportunities for members of our community. This position will offer various teaching opportunities throughout the year and will be responsible for developing and delivering accessible, engaging, and practical non-credit dance courses for participants of varying ages and experience levels. Dance Instructors may teach courses in a variety of styles and disciplines, including but not limited to ballroom, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, contemporary, cultural dance, line dancing, social dance, or other dance-related topics. Instructors will create a welcoming and supportive learning environment that encourages participants to develop their movement skills, confidence, creativity, physical wellness, and appreciation for dance. The instructor will be responsible for preparing lesson plans and course materials, demonstrating dance techniques and movements, providing clear instruction and feedback, and adapting activities to accommodate participants with varying skill levels and abilities. Courses should emphasize participation, personal enrichment, physical activity, and enjoyment while maintaining a safe and inclusive learning environment. Strong technical proficiency and the ability to demonstrate dance movements, techniques, and combinations clearly. Experience developing engaging, accessible, and inclusive lessons for participants with varying skill levels and abilities. Strong communication, interpersonal, and classroom management skills. Ability to create a positive, welcoming, and supportive learning environment. Experience working with adult learners, beginners, families, or community groups is preferred. Formal education, professional training, certifications, or demonstrated professional experience in dance or a related field preferred. Knowledge of safe movement practices, proper warm-up and cool-down techniques, and injury prevention. Ability to adapt instruction and activities to accommodate different physical abilities and learning styles. Commitment to providing enjoyable and enriching educational experiences that promote physical activity, confidence, creativity, and lifelong appreciation for dance. job_75168fc3d42f3c8b: The Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences Program at Princeton University, in association with NOAA's Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory (GFDL), seeks two postdoctoral or more senior research scientist for Earth System research and development activities focused on data science and engineering applied to stakeholder-relevant issues. Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham. Job Summary A postdoctoral position is available in the Division of Cardiovascular Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School in the NIH-funded laboratory of Dr. Farouc Jaffer. The postdoc’s focus; investigation of atherosclerosis inflammation using small and large animal models using novel molecular imaging approaches spanning intravascular microscopy to catheter-based intravascular imaging. A highly motivated, collaborative, critically thinking candidate is sought for a research fellowship that will investigate atherosclerosis in small and large animal disease models, utilizing intravital microscopy, cell biology, molecular pharmacology and physiology to understand the role of in vivo inflammation in atheroma disease progression and complication. Experience in atherosclerosis biology, surgical models, molecular biology (histopathology, RNA, cell culture), microscopy, and flow cytometry is desirable. We are seeking candidates with a PhD, MD/PhD, or MD with prior laboratory experience in biomedicine. Our interdisciplinary laboratory performs translational research, bridging the gap between understanding in vivo mechanisms of atheroma inflammation and the clinical goal of imaging coronary artery disease inflammation in patients for the first time in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. We focus on developing novel molecular imaging approaches to visualize high-risk plaques, vascular inflammation, and blood clots, including investigating blood flow restoration and therapeutic strategies to improve deep vein thrombosis resolution and prevent thrombotic syndrome. Another major focus is the use of intravital microscopy and intravascular imaging to study atherosclerosis and develop novel molecular imaging approaches. Recent trainees have published manuscripts in high-impact journals, presented at national and international conferences, won competitive fellowship awards, and have discovered new insights into how atheroma inflammation can be modulated by translational pharmacotherapeutic and coronary interventional devices. Recent trainees have attained faculty posts at prestigious academic institutions in the US, Korea, Japan, UK, Australia, and China, as well as senior scientist positions in the biotechnology and pharma industry.
